<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M⁺ at 233.96 Da) and the presence of a significant M+2 peak (~24 % of M), the compound likely contains one chlorine atom. The ¹³C NMR shows nine distinct carbon signals, including aromatic carbons (≈128–140 ppm) and aliphatic carbons at 49.4, 26.1, and 11.4 ppm, consistent with a chlorinated aromatic ring bearing a propyl side chain. A reasonable structure that fits these data is para‑chlorotert‑butylbenzene. Its SMILES representation is “Clc1ccc(cc1)C(C)(C)C”. This molecule has a molecular weight close to the observed value and matches the NMR pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)C(C)(C)C</final_answer>
